criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The purpose (monitoring GBR bleaching), the Australian benefit, and the primary users (marine and conservation scientists) are clear and supported by footnoted sources. However, mission goals, objectives and quantified requirements are not stated, and the functional link to the space segment is thin. Other users such as reef managers are not identified. Some claims are unreferenced, so this sits at Adequate.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A week-by-week Gantt chart covers all major tasks with dates, status colours and task descriptions, and it is clearly feasible. Information sources are listed as links. However, there is no explicit contingency or variation provision for slipped tasks, and the plan is not tied explicitly to the mission narrative. Adequate fits best.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
Week 10 is reserved for review, amendments, final simulations, and reflection.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Work to date is limited to literature review, reading a bleaching-monitoring brief and completing STK tutorials. No technical results are presented, such as orbit parameters, coverage, ground-track or link calculations, or STK outputs. Progress is minor and cannot yet be judged as clearly on track, so Adequate low is appropriate.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure is logical with clear headings, writing is mostly fluent and the Gantt chart is readable. Footnote citations are used. However, the Gantt chart has no figure caption, the red deadline lines are hard to see, the footnotes and Useful Links list do not map one-to-one, and some wording is informal or awkward.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue.

technical_issues.issue: Ocean acidification is presented as the cause of coral bleaching. Bleaching is driven mainly by thermal stress, so the causal chain is misstated.
The claim that current satellites map GBR depths only to 100 m per pixel is unreferenced and may be inaccurate; the cited source does not support a direct comparison with the proposed mission.
Mission requirements are absent: no orbit regime, altitude, payload, coverage or latency target is given, so the concept cannot be linked to space-segment design.
The statement that hundreds of millions of humans rely on reefs is unreferenced, and the 30% acidity figure is loosely phrased without the pH or H+ basis.

overall: A sensible, Australia-focused reef-monitoring concept with a feasible Gantt plan and a reasonable reference set. Weaknesses are the lack of stated mission requirements and orbit/space-segment linkage, very thin technical progress, a causal error on acidification and bleaching, and minor inconsistencies in referencing and figure captioning.

feedback.summary: You have built a sensible, Australia-focused reef-monitoring concept with a clear, feasible week-by-week Gantt plan and a reasonable set of references. The main gaps are stated mission requirements, a link from the concept to space-segment design, a corrected acidification and bleaching explanation, and some technical results. Addressing these would move several criteria up a level.
next_steps: Correct the acidification and bleaching causal chain, and verify or remove the unreferenced claims about the 100 m pixel comparison and the hundreds-of-millions figure.
Write a concise requirements table covering orbit regime, altitude, payload, coverage and latency, and trace each requirement to your mission goals and user needs.
Produce your first STK results, such as orbit parameters or ground-track outputs, with a short interpretation, and add contingency provisions for slipped tasks to your Gantt plan.

criteria.C1: Your purpose of monitoring Great Barrier Reef bleaching and your primary users, marine and conservation scientists, are clear and footnoted. To reach Accomplished, state quantified mission requirements (orbit, altitude, payload, coverage, latency) and link them to space-segment design. Identify further users such as reef managers. Correct the claim that acidification causes bleaching, since thermal stress is the main driver, and reference or remove the unsupported claims.
criteria.C2: Your week-by-week Gantt chart covers all major tasks with dates, status colours and descriptions, and the plan is clearly feasible. Week 10 is reserved for review, which is a good decision. To reach Accomplished, add explicit contingency and variation provisions for slipped or extended tasks, and explain why the sequencing suits the mission narrative. Ensure each information source is cited consistently.
criteria.C3: You have completed a literature review, read the bleaching-monitoring brief and finished STK tutorials 1 to 4. No technical results are yet presented. To reach Accomplished, include a good set of preliminary results, for example STK orbit parameters, coverage or ground-track outputs, each with a brief interpretation showing you are on track for completion.
criteria.C4: Your report has a logical structure with clear headings, and the writing is mostly fluent. The Gantt chart is readable, but it lacks a figure caption and its red deadline lines are hard to see. Footnote citations do not map one-to-one to the Useful Links list, and some wording is informal. To reach Accomplished, caption all figures, improve contrast, align references with the list, and polish the language.
